topic: Ownership transition confirmed (National Grid -> Centrica/ECP, Aug 2025)
wiki_text: On 14 August 2025 National Grid plc announced, and subsequently completed, the sale of its Grain LNG business (Isle of Grain, Kent - the UK's largest LNG import terminal) to a 50/50 consortium of Centrica plc and Energy Capital Partners (ECP, part of Bridgepoint Group plc) for ~GBP 1.66 billion (including ~GBP 1.1bn of new non-recourse project finance; Centrica's equity ~GBP 200m). This confirms GEM's current ownership record (Owner: Centrica PLC 50% / Energy Capital Partners 50%; Parent chain Centrica / Bridgepoint Group). The terminal continues to operate under long-term take-or-pay capacity contracts (e.g. QatarEnergy's 25-year deal from mid-2025). No further ownership change is required in GEM.

The Grain LNG expansion (GEM 8.7 mtpa unit) raises site storage to 1.2 million m3 and regasification/redelivery to ~800 GWh/d, and adds a second cryogenic unloading line - making Grain the only European terminal able to perform simultaneous LNG unloads. The expansion was scheduled to come on stream from mid-July 2025; the 2025 GIIGNL report had it still under construction in late 2024 but on track for the mid-2025 launch. Post-expansion total terminal capacity is ~23 mtpa. Status of the expansion unit should be re-checked against GIIGNL 2026 / operator pages to confirm whether it is now operating (see qa).

topic: Crown LNG Grangemouth timeline (and Kakinada confusion)
wiki_text: Crown LNG Holdings (Nasdaq: CGBS) is developing an FSRU-based import terminal in the Firth of Forth at Grangemouth (~5 mtpa, ~USD 533m, intended to supply a gas-fired power plant). Crown acquired the Grangemouth terminal assets, selected IKM Consulting as engineering design partner (2024), and is progressing consenting with the Scottish/UK governments. FID guidance for Grangemouth slipped from late-2024 to a Q2-2025 target, with first operation 'at the earliest' 2027. CAUTION when updating GEM: the widely-cited 'FID 2026 / first gas 2029' figures belong to Crown's separate Kakinada (India) gravity-based-structure project, not Grangemouth. As of this sweep there is no confirmation the Q2-2025 Grangemouth FID actually closed, so FIDYear=2025 in GEM may be optimistic (see qa).
